Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-bf9d5c44: shift foreground down one row

## Confirmed transformation
For this task ID, translate every non-background cell in the entire input grid down exactly one row. Vacated cells in the top row become background; foreground cells shifted beyond the bottom edge are clipped/discarded. Preserve all colors and all relative positions among foreground cells. Output dimensions remain exactly the same.

Equivalent procedure: initialize output as a copy of the input; set row 0 to the background color; for every original cell at `(r,c)` with `r < height-1`, copy it to `(r+1,c)`. The original last row has no destination and its foreground cells are dropped. Derive the background from the current instance, rather than assuming a particular color.

## Evidence
A demo pair (8x21, background 8, foreground 5) showed the exact one-row downward translation: output row 0 was background, rows 1–7 matched input rows 0–6, and the input's foreground cells on row 7 were clipped. The transformation was then applied to a 29x27 test (background 3, foreground 9) and accepted correct on the first submission (zero wrong attempts).

## Validation

- Ensure the top row is entirely background.
